{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_1e6283f56e17438abf5081b6","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# gantry — Application Plan\n2\t\n3\t*Last updated: 2026-07-22. Revision history lives in git; decision provenance in `docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md`.*\n4\t\n5\t## Overview\n6\t\n7\t`gantry` is a transparent offload shim for expensive developer commands, cargo-first. A shim binary named `cargo` sits ahead of the real toolchain in PATH; when an intercepted subcommand (default: `test`) is run inside a clean, pushable git repo, gantry ships the exact commit to a pluggable remote executor, streams logs back, and returns a faithful exit code. In every other case it runs the command locally under a cgroup resource cap. Callers — humans, scripts, AI agent fleets — never change what they type.\n8\t\n9\tExtraction and hardening of the in-house `~/.local/bin/cargo` + `cargo-remote` bash pair (see `docs/research/in-house-implementation.md`); packaging follows the single-static-binary + installer + `doctor` pattern surveyed in `docs/research/prior-art.md`.\n10\t\n11\t## Goals\n12\t\n13\t1. Drop-in transparency: `cargo test` keeps working everywhere, with zero caller-side changes.\n14\t2. Never lose a test result: every invocation ends in a real verdict (remote or capped-local), every degradation is printed and logged.\n15\t3. Never mutate branch state: code sync uses hidden content-addressed refs only.\n16\t4. Pluggable remote execution: Argo Workflows first-class, generic command-template backend for everyone else, SSH later.\n17\t5. Protect the shared machine: production-proven cgroup caps on all local execution paths.\n18\t6. Publishable quality: single static binary, installer, `doctor`, docs that stand alone without this infrastructure.\n19\t\n20\t## Non-goals\n21\t\n22\tCompilation caching (compose with sccache), hermetic/Bazel-style execution, dirty-tree syncing, per-agent hook integrations, Windows, nextest interception (v1). See `docs/notes/features.md` for rationale.\n23\t\n24\t## Terms & conventions\n25\t\n26\t**Normative language:** MUST / MUST NOT are binding — violating them fails this spec. SHOULD means deviation requires a documented reason. MAY is truly optional.\n27\t\n28\t**Glossary** (two uses of \"gate\" exist; they are different things):\n29\t- **shim** — the binary installed under the name `cargo`, ahead of the real toolchain in PATH.\n30\t- **intercepted / passthrough** — an invocation gantry may offload vs. one it forwards untouched (under the cap when `cap_passthrough`).\n31\t- **GitGate** — the *eligibility* checks (work tree, HEAD, remote, clean) deciding remote vs. local. Never called just \"gate\" in output.\n32\t- **quality gate** — an opt-in remote check beyond the caller's argv (clippy, fmt), always labeled `[gantry] gate:` and carrying verdict `gate_failure` when failed.\n33\t- **verdict** — the terminal classification of a run (`pass` / `test_failure` / `gate_failure` / `infra_failure` / `cancelled` / `superseded`). The exit code is derived from it, never vice versa.\n34\t- **Tier-0** — zero-config mode: cap-only, nothing goes remote.\n35\t- **backend / preset** — a `RemoteBackend` implementation vs. a shipped configuration of one (SSH is a preset of `command`).\n36\t- **fallback / degradation** — the loud, recorded switch to a capped local run after an infra failure or gate ineligibility.\n37\t- **epoch ref / lease** — `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` plus the client-side record that protects it from GC while a run is live.\n38\t- **attachment / waiter** — a process streaming/waiting on a run (originator or JoinTable joiner).\n39\t\n40\t**Scope lock:** v1 scope is frozen as of 2026-07-22 (17 adopted mechanisms; see Resolved questions). New scope enters only via the ideation ledger → plan amendment → commit, *before* implementation of that item begins. In-flight scope additions are forbidden — this plan doubled in mechanism count across two productive ideation days precisely because the pipeline works; the freeze is what makes Phase 1 finishable.\n41\t\n42\t## Acceptance scenarios\n43\t\n44\tNamed scenarios define \"done.\" Each is independently verifiable; phase acceptance lists reference them.\n45\t\n46\t**AS-1 Happy path (human).** A developer in a clean, pushed-up repo runs `cargo test`. → gantry pushes the epoch ref, submits, streams logs live, prints the verdict trailer. → Exit 0 on pass.\n47\t*Pass:* zero caller-side changes; logs stream within 30s of submit or a queue explanation prints; exit code equals what local `cargo test` would have produced.\n48\t*Fail:* any branch ref moved on the remote; silence >60s with no `[gantry]` line; exit code differs from the suite's true result.\n49\t\n50\t**AS-2 Agent machine-mode (primary audience).** A NEEDLE worker (`GANTRY_AGENT=1`) runs `cargo test` on a wip branch; the suite has one failing test. → Remote runs, verdict `test_failure` with `failure_class: test-failure`. → The worker runs `gantry why --json` and branches on the failure class without parsing logs.\n51\t*Pass:* transcript contains the decision line, verdict trailer, and handle; `why --json` parses with a stable schema and names the failure class; the worker never needed a human.\n52\t*Fail:* worker must regex the log stream to learn what happened; JSON schema drifts between invocations; a gate failure is indistinguishable from a test failure.\n53\t\n54\t**AS-3 Cluster outage under fleet load.** 20 agents run `cargo test` while the backend is unreachable. → Every run prints the infra reason, acquires a fallback slot (max 3 concurrent), and runs capped locally; the rest queue loudly.\n55\t*Pass:* box load stays bounded (slice cap holds); every run ends in a real verdict; runs.jsonl shows 20 intent+verdict pairs with `ran: local_after_infra`.\n56\t*Fail:* simultaneous uncapped local builds (the meltdown gantry exists to prevent); any run exits with neither verdict nor orphan record.\n57\t\n58\t**AS-4 Dirty tree.** A developer with an uncommitted new test file runs `cargo test`. → GitGate blocks remote (untracked file detected), prints the reason and the exact two-command path to eligibility, runs capped locally.\n59\t*Pass:* the untracked file's tests actually ran (locally); reason `dirty` recorded; no ref pushed.\n60\t*Fail:* remote runs against code missing the new file (the predecessor's silent-gap bug); user must read docs to learn why it ran locally.\n61\t\n62\t**AS-5 Gate failure attribution.** Gates enabled (fleet config); tests pass but clippy fails. → Exit non-zero with verdict `gate_failure`, output attributing the failure to `[gantry] gate: clippy`, tests reported green.\n63\t*Pass:* an agent reading `why --json` sees tests-passed-gate-failed and fixes lints, not tests.\n64\t*Fail:* gate failure presented as a test failure (misdirected agent work), or gates-off runs affected in any way.\n65\t\n66\t**Success metrics:** *Performance* — passthrough <5ms p99; submit overhead (gate+push+submit, excluding queue) ≤5s p50. *Functionality* — AS-1..AS-5 pass. *Adoption* — one week of NEEDLE traffic with zero silent skips and ≥90% of eligible runs offloaded; bash pair deleted.\n67\t\n68\t## Architecture\n69\t\n70\t```\n71\tcaller (human / agent / script)\n72\t   │  runs `cargo test …`\n73\t   ▼\n74\t[shim dir]/cargo ──symlink──► gantry binary\n75\t   │  argv[0]=cargo → tool profile \"cargo\"\n76\t   ├─ subcommand not intercepted ───────────────► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n77\t   ├─ GANTRY_LOCAL=1 / disabled / Tier-0 (no config) ──► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n78\t   ▼\n79\tDecisionEngine\n80\t   ├─ GitGate: work tree? remote? clean (porcelain)? HEAD?\n81\t   │     └─ any \"no\" → LocalExecutor (reason printed)\n82\t   ▼\n83\tRefPusher: git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>  (+ lease, + GC sweep)\n84\t   ▼\n85\tBackend (trait RemoteBackend)\n86\t   ├─ argo:    create Workflow(templateRef, params) → stream pod logs → poll status.phase\n87\t   ├─ command: run user-templated submit/logs/wait argv arrays\n88\t   └─ ssh preset: command-template preset + contrib/gantry-exec.sh (flagship onboarding)\n89\t   ▼\n90\tVerdict\n91\t   ├─ Pass ──────────────► exit 0\n92\t   ├─ TestFailure ───────► exit code (no local retry — DD-4)\n93\t   ├─ GateFailure ───────► exit non-zero, attributed to `[gantry] gate:` (no retry)\n94\t   └─ InfraFailure ──────► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n95\t                                   │\n96\t                          RunLog (~/.local/state/gantry/runs.jsonl)\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\tCross-cutting: `RunLog` records every decision; `Locks/JoinTable` (v1.x) dedups concurrent identical runs; `doctor` validates the whole chain.\n100\t\n101\t## Components\n102\t\n103\t### 1. Shim & dispatcher (`main.rs`)\n104\t- Dispatch on `argv[0]`: `cargo` → cargo tool profile; `gantry` → management CLI (full command set defined once in the “CLI surface” section below).\n105\t- Real-binary resolution: config override `real_binary`, else PATH lookup with gantry's own shim dir stripped (self-recursion guard: refuse to exec a path whose canonical target is the gantry binary).\n106\t- Passthrough path budget: no git/network/config-parse beyond a single mmap'd config read; target < 5 ms overhead.\n107\t\n108\t### 2. DecisionEngine\n109\t- Intercept set from config (`[tool.cargo] intercept = [\"test\"]`).\n110\t- Tier-0 (zero-config): with no config file present or `backend = \"none\"`, gantry is a pure local cap-wrapper — interception still applies the cgroup cap and full RunLog, nothing goes remote, and a `[gantry]` line notes the tier at most once per hour (state-file timestamp) so transcripts see it without per-run noise. Install→value with zero setup; remote offload is an upgrade, not a prerequisite.\n111\t- Kill switches: `GANTRY_LOCAL=1`, `gantry off` (state file).\n112\t- Config-failure policy (resolves Q-7 via last-known-good): on parse failure, serve the persisted last-good config snapshot from the state dir and print an escalating `[gantry] config broken since <ts>, N runs degraded` banner on every intercepted run until fixed; with no snapshot, fail open to plain passthrough with the same banner. Behavior is never derived from a half-parsed file — a broken gantry must never block builds, and must never rot silently either.\n113\t\n114\t### 3. GitGate\n115\t- Checks in order, each with a printed reason on failure: inside work tree → `HEAD` resolves → configured remote exists → `git status --porcelain` empty.\n116\t- All git interaction shells out to system `git` (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior, honors user's git config/credentials/hooks).\n117\t\n118\t### 4. RefPusher\n119\t- `git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` (`ci_remote` defaults to `origin`); the epoch prefix is the GC lever (see below).\n120\t- Push failure = InfraFailure → local fallback.\n121\t- Optional `push_mode = \"branch\"` legacy escape hatch (explicit opt-in; prints a warning naming the risk).\n122\t- GC (resolves Q-3 via leases): refs are named `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`; each run records a client-side lease (ref, run-id, expiry) in the state dir, and every successful push opportunistically sweeps remote refs whose epoch has expired and whose runs are terminal — no cron, no daemon, and a sweep can never delete a ref an in-flight run still holds a lease on. Each box sweeps only refs it created — lease records are local (see EC-09). The epoch-vs-content-addressing tension (the same sha pushed twice yields two refs) is settled by the design note required at Phase 1a entry.\n123\t\n124\t### 5. RemoteBackend trait + implementations\n125\t\n126\t```rust\n127\ttrait RemoteBackend {\n128\t    fn submit(&self, spec: &RunSpec) -> Result<RunHandle, BackendError>;\n129\t    fn stream_logs(&self, h: &RunHandle, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<(), BackendError>; // best-effort\n130\t    fn wait(&self, h: &RunHandle, deadline: Instant) -> Result<Verdict, BackendError>;     // authoritative\n131\t    fn describe(&self, h: &RunHandle) -> String;  // human URL/name for \"see details at …\"\n132\t    fn cancel(&self, h: &RunHandle) -> Result<(), BackendError>;                            // Ctrl-C propagation\n133\t}\n134\t```\n135\t\n136\t- **`argo`** (v1): builds the Workflow manifest with serde (no string splicing), submits via `kubectl create -f -` (kubeconfig path from config; direct REST API is a later option), polls pods for streaming, polls `status.phase` for the verdict, falls back to reading `outputs.parameters.output` when podGC ate the logs. Ships `contrib/argo/gantry-verify-workflowtemplate.yml` — a genericized `rust-verify` (parameters: `repo`, `revision`, `args-json`, `builder-image`; sccache optional). Remote contract (resolves Q-2 as faithful-argv): the remote executes exactly the argv the caller typed; check/clippy run only as opt-in quality gates from trusted user config, reported as separately-labeled `[gantry] gate:` results, never conflated with the test verdict. A failing enabled gate yields verdict `gate_failure`: overall exit is non-zero (agents must see red), output and records attribute it to the named gate, and — like TestFailure — it never triggers a local retry. The template also emits a structured `verdict.json` output parameter — one versioned schema (`schema_version`, phase, exit code, oom, deadline from workflow node status, plus an optional `failure_class`: compile-error vs test-failure vs doctest vs harness-panic, derived from cargo's stable `--message-format json` stream) — so OOMKilled and deadline-exceeded classify as InfraFailure → fallback, never TestFailure, and agents branch on failure class without parsing logs. Consumers ignore unknown fields; an absent verdict.json degrades gracefully to exit-code-only interpretation (command templates). Parity preflight: builder images carry capability labels (`org.gantry.toolchain=…`); before submission gantry compares local rust-toolchain.toml and requested features against them — a mismatch is a loud local fallback (warn-only for unlabeled images), because a verdict from the wrong toolchain is a wrong answer delivered confidently.\n137\t- **`command`** (v1): three user-configured argv arrays (`submit`, `logs`, `wait`) with `{repo}` `{rev}` `{args_json}` `{handle}` placeholder substitution at the argv level; `submit`'s stdout is the handle; `wait`'s exit code is the verdict (0 pass, 1 test-failure, ≥2 infra-failure — documented contract).\n138\t- **SSH-first onboarding** (v1, flagship): not a third backend implementation — a shipped command-template *preset* plus `contrib/gantry-exec.sh` (~150-line POSIX executor that clones `refs/gantry/*` and runs the command), which doubles as executable documentation of the remote contract. \"Remote = any spare SSH box\" is the documented quickstart path; Argo is the \"advanced\" backend. A native `ssh` backend remains possible later only if the preset proves limiting.\n139\t\n140\t### 6. LocalExecutor\n141\t- `systemd-run --scope --user -p CPUQuota={n}% -p MemoryMax={m} -p MemorySwapMax=0 -q -- <real> <args…>`; on failure to create a scope (no user session / container), plain `exec`.\n142\t- Applies to: intercepted-command fallbacks always; all passthrough invocations when `cap_passthrough = true` (default, matching predecessor).\n143\t- Fallback admission semaphore: capped local *fallback* runs additionally acquire a flock-based token file (default 3 concurrent per box) and queue with loud `[gantry] waiting for local slot (N ahead)` lines and a bounded wait — a remote outage under ~20 agents degrades as a serialized trickle, not a stampede that recreates the meltdown gantry exists to prevent. Kernel lock release means a SIGKILLed agent can never leak a slot.\n144\t- Boxwide slice: every gantry-spawned local run lands in one systemd user slice (`gantry.slice`) carrying a box-level *sum* cap (configurable, e.g. 12 CPU / 32G) alongside the per-run caps — the semaphore bounds the count, the slice bounds the total; 20 × \"200%/6G each\" can no longer add up past the machine. Degrades cleanly where slices are unavailable.\n145\t- Agent-priority queueing: `GANTRY_AGENT=1` (env convention — deliberately not TTY sniffing, since tmux-hosted agents have TTYs) orders the fallback-semaphore queue humans-first, agents-behind, with a printed triage tag (any future submission gating inherits the same ordering).\n146\t\n147\t### 7. RunLog & UX\n148\t- stderr lines prefixed `[gantry]`: decision, workflow name/URL, fallback reason, verdict. Written for agent transcripts as much as humans.\n149\t- `~/.local/state/gantry/runs.jsonl`: write-ahead form — an OPEN intent record is appended *before* dispatch, and every exit path must append a matching terminal verdict record; `gantry doctor` flags orphaned OPEN records as lost runs, making a silently-skipped run structurally detectable rather than an absence of evidence. O_APPEND single-line writes for concurrency safety.\n150\t- Intent records capture all gate inputs (tree state, remote, kill-switch state, chosen backend) so `gantry why` can replay the decision truthfully after the fact.\n151\t- Flight recorder: every InfraFailure snapshots a redacted diagnostic bundle (config snapshot, git state, raw backend response, recent stderr) to `~/.local/state/gantry/crash/<run-id>/`; `gantry report <run-id>` prints or packages it. Infra flakes become post-mortem-able artifacts instead of archaeology; the redaction list is load-bearing and conservative by default.\n152\t\n153\t### 8. doctor / installer\n154\t- `gantry doctor`: shim-before-real PATH ordering; real binary resolves and is not gantry; config parses; backend preflight (`kubectl` reachable / template exists, or command-backend binaries exist); systemd-run scope creation probe; git identity present; orphaned intent records reported as lost runs.\n155\t- `gantry doctor --e2e`: canary run — pushes a tiny known-good fixture ref through the real RefPusher and backend and asserts the expected pass verdict round-trips. One command answers \"is the pipeline actually working\" on the operator's schedule, not at 9am when 20 agents degrade. Mechanism: pushes the current repo's HEAD as a normal gantry ref but overrides the argv with a trivial command (`cargo --version`), exercising push → clone → contract → verdict without running a real suite; `gantry init --ssh` runs it as its final step.\n156\t- `gantry doctor --drill`: fault-injection fire drill — injects a synthetic InfraFailure through a drill-scoped hook (never honored outside a drill) and asserts the entire loud-degrade chain fires: banner, intent/verdict records, semaphore-gated capped local run, correct exit code. The fallback path is gantry's core safety promise and otherwise only executes when things are already on fire.\n157\t- `install.sh`: detect platform → fetch release binary → install to `~/.local/bin/gantry` → create shim symlink(s) in a configured shim dir → verify PATH ordering (instruct if wrong) → write starter config → run `doctor`. `gantry uninstall` reverses it.\n158\t- Onboarding must be smooth and automatic: `gantry init --ssh user@host` performs the whole SSH-first setup — verifies git+cargo on the target, writes the command-template preset config, and finishes with `doctor --e2e`. Install to first remote run in ~10 minutes, no Kubernetes required.\n159\t\n160\t### 9. JoinTable (v1.x)\n161\t- Key: `(remote_url, sha, tool, args)` hash. A flock'd state dir maps in-flight keys → RunHandle; a second invocation attaches to the existing handle (stream + wait) instead of resubmitting.\n162\t\n163\t### 10. Ledger intelligence (v1.x)\n164\tOne verdict-history module over runs.jsonl powering three features:\n165\t- **Memoization (opt-in, never default):** an identical `(tree-hash, args, toolchain, image digest)` with a terminal PASS verdict returns the recorded verdict instantly with a `[gantry] cached` line and a `--fresh` escape. Keyed on tree hash, not commit sha, so rebases/amends with identical trees still hit. Failures are never memoized.\n166\t- **Supersede-on-new-commit:** a newer sha submitted for the same (repo, args) cancels the older still-running sibling with an explicit `superseded` terminal record — recorded, never silent — reclaiming cluster minutes from fast-iterating agents. Supersede never yanks a watched run: it applies only when the older run has zero live attachments (originator gone, no JoinTable waiters); otherwise the newer sha simply runs alongside.\n167\t- **Flake flagging:** the same tree + args with flipping verdicts marks runs `flaky-suspect` in runs.jsonl and the stderr summary.\n168\t\n169\t### Proposed module layout\n170\t\n171\t```\n172\tsrc/main.rs            argv[0] dispatch only\n173\tsrc/shim.rs            passthrough fast path (<5ms budget lives here)\n174\tsrc/decision.rs        intercept set, Tier-0, kill switches\n175\tsrc/gate.rs            GitGate\n176\tsrc/refs.rs            RefPusher: epoch refs, leases, GC sweep\n177\tsrc/backend/mod.rs     RemoteBackend trait + verdict.json parsing\n178\tsrc/backend/argo.rs    kubectl-based Argo backend\n179\tsrc/backend/command.rs command-template backend (SSH preset = config + contrib script)\n180\tsrc/local.rs           LocalExecutor: scope, slice, semaphore, priority\n181\tsrc/runlog.rs          write-ahead ledger, flight recorder\n182\tsrc/config.rs          layering, last-known-good, trust boundary\n183\tsrc/cli/               doctor, why, explain, init, quickcheck, report, status…\n184\tcontrib/argo/          reference WorkflowTemplate\n185\tcontrib/gantry-exec.sh shell reference executor\n186\ttests/properties/      argv round-trip, ref-name fuzzing\n187\ttests/stampede/        20-way concurrency harness\n188\ttests/e2e/             drill + canary fixtures\n189\t```\n190\t\n191\t## Data models\n192\t\n193\t### Config — `~/.config/gantry/config.toml` (layered: /etc/gantry → user → repo `.gantry.toml`)\n194\t\n195\t```toml\n196\t[local]\n197\tcpu_quota_pct = 200\n198\tmemory_max    = \"6G\"\n199\tcap_passthrough = true\n200\t\n201\t[tool.cargo]\n202\tintercept   = [\"test\"]\n203\t# real_binary = \"/home/user/.cargo/bin/cargo\"   # optional override\n204\t\n205\t[remote]\n206\tbackend    = \"none\"          # none = Tier-0 cap-only (zero-config default) | argo | command\n207\tci_remote  = \"origin\"\n208\tpush_mode  = \"ref\"           # ref | branch (legacy, warns)\n209\tdeadline_minutes = 40\n210\t\n211\t[remote.argo]\n212\tkubeconfig = \"~/.kube/config\"\n213\tnamespace  = \"argo-workflows\"\n214\ttemplate   = \"gantry-verify\"\n215\tgenerate_name = \"gantry-\"\n216\t\n217\t[remote.command]\n218\t# submit = [\"my-ci\", \"submit\", \"--repo\", \"{repo}\", \"--rev\", \"{rev}\", \"--args\", \"{args_json}\"]\n219\t# logs   = [\"my-ci\", \"logs\", \"{handle}\", \"--follow\"]\n220\t# wait   = [\"my-ci\", \"wait\", \"{handle}\"]\n221\t```\n222\t\n223\tRepo-level `.gantry.toml` may narrow behavior (add intercepts, set `backend = \"none\"`) but may **not** change `ci_remote`/`push_mode`/credential-adjacent keys — repo config is data from the repo, and a cloned repo must not be able to redirect pushes (security consideration S-2).\n224\t\n225\t### RunSpec / RunRecord\n226\t\n227\t```rust\n228\tstruct RunSpec { tool: String, subcommand: String, args: Vec<String>,\n229\t                 repo_url: String, sha: String, cwd_rel: PathBuf }\n230\t```\n231\t\n232\t`cwd_rel` is the caller's directory relative to the repo root; remote executors `cd` into it before running the argv, so workspace-member invocations behave identically remote and local.\n233\t\n234\t```rust\n235\t// runs.jsonl — write-ahead: one OPEN intent + one terminal record per invocation\n236\t{ \"rec\": \"intent\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"run_id\": \"01J…\", \"ts\": …,\n237\t  \"tool\": \"cargo\", \"args\": [\"test\",\"--\",\"--nocapture\"], \"repo\": \"…\", \"sha\": \"…\", \"cwd_rel\": \".\",\n238\t  \"gate\": { \"worktree\": true, \"head\": true, \"remote\": true, \"clean\": true },\n239\t  \"decision\": \"remote|local\", \"reason\": \"clean|dirty|no_remote|tier0|disabled|env\",\n240\t  \"backend\": \"argo|command|none\" }\n241\t{ \"rec\": \"verdict\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"run_id\": \"01J…\", \"ts\": …,\n242\t  \"verdict\": \"pass|test_failure|gate_failure|infra_failure|superseded|cancelled\",\n243\t  \"ran\": \"remote|local|local_after_infra\", \"exit_code\": 0, \"handle\": \"gantry-x7k2p\",\n244\t  \"durations_ms\": { \"gate\": 40, \"push\": 900, \"queue\": 12000, \"run\": 341000 } }\n245\t```\n246\t\n247\t### Verdict semantics (the load-bearing enum)\n248\t\n249\t| Verdict | Meaning | Action |\n250\t|---|---|---|\n251\t| `Pass` | remote ran suite, passed | exit 0 |\n252\t| `TestFailure` | remote ran suite, failed | exit non-zero; **no local retry** |\n253\t| `InfraFailure` | no verdict produced (push/submit/schedule/stream/deadline) | capped local run; its exit code wins |\n254\t\n255\tOOMKilled pods and deadline-exceeded workflows are `InfraFailure` by definition (via the remote contract's `verdict.json`): an infrastructure cap firing says nothing about the code, and reporting it as a test failure would fake a result.\n256\t\n257\tTerminal-record values extend the ladder: `gate_failure` (an enabled quality gate failed while tests passed — exit non-zero, attribution to the named gate, no local retry), `cancelled` (user Ctrl-C), and `superseded` (v1.x, see Ledger intelligence). `verdict` applies to local runs too (`ran: \"local\"`); an infra fallback records the final local outcome as `ran: \"local_after_infra\"`.\n258\t\n259\t### Versioning & compatibility\n260\t\n261\tEvery machine-consumed surface carries an explicit version; unknown fields are always ignored (additive evolution is free, removal/retyping is a major bump):\n262\t\n263\t- **runs.jsonl** — `schema_version` on every record. Readers MUST tolerate newer minor records; `gantry doctor` flags a ledger written by a newer major.\n264\t- **verdict.json** — `schema_version`; absent file = exit-code-only contract. Optional fields (`failure_class`) are exactly that.\n265\t- **`--json` CLI output** (`why`/`explain`/`status`) — top-level `schema_version`; the JSON surface is the primary interface, human text is a rendering of it.\n266\t- **Remote contract** — the client sends `contract_version` as a workflow parameter; the template echoes it in verdict.json. A mismatch the client can't interpret = InfraFailure with an explicit \"contract drift\" message, never a misread verdict. Template upgrades are blue-green: `gantry-verify` versions coexist and the client config pins one.\n267\t- **Config** — unknown keys warn (never error); renamed keys keep a one-major deprecation alias; the last-known-good snapshot stores the schema version it parsed under.\n268\t- **Backward-compat stance for the predecessor:** cap values and nextest non-interception match the bash pair exactly; behavioral differences (porcelain gate, epoch refs, OOM classification) are deliberate fixes, listed in the migration notes — there is no bug-for-bug mode.\n269\t\n270\t## CLI surface\n271\t\n272\t```\n273\tcargo <anything>            # via shim — the entire point\n274\tgantry doctor [--e2e|--drill]        # verify install; canary the real pipeline; fire-drill the fallback chain\n275\tgantry init --ssh user@host          # automatic SSH-first onboarding (preset + contrib executor + e2e check)\n276\tgantry why                  # replay the last run's gate/decision trace (\"clean tree: NO ← here\")\n277\tgantry explain -- <cmd…>    # dry run: what WOULD happen (gates, backend, exact ref) — no network\n278\tgantry on | off             # global toggle (state file)\n279\tgantry run [--backend B] -- <cmd…>   # explicit offload, no shim needed (v1.x)\n280\tgantry status               # recent runs, in-flight runs\n281\tgantry quickcheck           # 30s no-backend sanity: shim resolves, cap works, git ok (Tier-0 proof)\n282\tgantry report <run-id>      # print/package the flight-recorder bundle for an InfraFailure\n283\tgantry install-shims | uninstall\n284\tgantry config [--show-origin]\n285\tgantry version\n286\t```\n287\t\n288\tDiagnostics are agent-first: `why`, `explain`, and `status` take `--json` with a stable schema, so a fleet agent that hits a degradation can explore and self-diagnose (why did this run locally? is the remote down for everyone?) without a human reading stderr.\n289\t\n290\t## Failure modes (exhaustive, each with defined behavior)\n291\t\n292\t| Failure | Class | Behavior |\n293\t|---|---|---|\n294\t| not a git repo / no remote / dirty / untracked files | eligibility (GitGate) | local capped run, reason printed |\n295\t| ref push rejected (auth, network) | infra | local capped run |\n296\t| submit error (kubectl/exec fails) | infra | local capped run |\n297\t| pod never scheduled by deadline | infra | **local capped run** (predecessor wrongly exited 1) |\n298\t| log stream lost mid-run | infra (recoverable) | keep waiting on status; fetch output param at end |\n299\t| client deadline (`deadline_minutes`) exceeded | infra | print handle URL, local capped run |\n300\t| remote suite fails | test | exit non-zero, stop |\n301\t| enabled quality gate fails (tests pass) | quality-gate | exit non-zero, verdict `gate_failure` attributed to the named gate; no local retry |\n302\t| remote pod OOMKilled / workflow `activeDeadlineSeconds` exceeded | infra | `verdict.json` classifies as InfraFailure → capped local run — never reported as a test failure |\n303\t| gantry process killed mid-run | self | orphaned OPEN intent in runs.jsonl; `gantry doctor` reports it as a lost run |\n304\t| remote outage → mass fallback | env | admission semaphore caps concurrent local runs (default 3), loud queue-position lines |\n305\t| Ctrl-C during remote run | user | propagate `cancel()`, exit 130 |\n306\t| gantry config broken/missing | self | serve last-known-good snapshot + escalating banner; plain passthrough if no snapshot (never silent) |\n307\t| systemd-run unavailable | env | plain exec (documented: containers self-limit) |\n308\t| gantry binary deleted but shim remains | self | shim *is* the binary (symlink) — impossible state; doctor checks dangling links |\n309\t\n310\t## Edge case catalog\n311\t\n312\t**EC-01 Linked git worktrees (load-bearing: NEEDLE workers share worktrees).** All GitGate checks and pushes operate on the *worktree's* HEAD and index. JoinTable and memoization keys use the common git dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) + sha, so two worktrees of one repo dedup correctly. A stampede-test variant MUST run from two worktrees of the same repo.\n313\t\n314\t**EC-02 Detached HEAD.** Eligible — a sha is a sha. The decision line notes `(detached)`; nothing else differs.\n315\t\n316\t**EC-03 Submodules.** If `.gitmodules` exists, v1 falls back locally with reason `submodules` (the remote clone contract doesn't recurse yet). Loud, honest, and cheap; recursion is a template upgrade later.\n317\t\n318\t**EC-04 Shallow local clone.** Push of the epoch ref may fail against a shallow history → ordinary push InfraFailure → capped local run. No special handling; the reason line names the likely cause.\n319\t\n320\t**EC-05 Huge repo / slow status.** `git status --porcelain` on a monorepo can take seconds. Gate duration is recorded (`durations_ms.gate`) and a `[gantry] slow gate (Ns) — consider .gitignore hygiene` hint prints past 2s. The gate is never skipped for speed.\n321\t\n322\t**EC-06 Pathological argv.** NULs are impossible in argv; newlines/quotes/100KB args MUST round-trip byte-exact (property test, tests/properties/). Args are never shell-interpolated anywhere (S-4).\n323\t\n324\t**EC-07 Cargo aliases and bare `cargo`.** Interception matches argv[1] exactly against the intercept set. Aliases expanding to `test` inside real cargo are NOT intercepted (documented limitation — gantry never parses cargo config to chase aliases).\n325\t\n326\t**EC-08 State dir unwritable / disk full.** Never blocks the build: run proceeds with in-memory records, one warning line, and `doctor` reports the unwritable state dir. A full disk MUST NOT turn into a missing verdict or a crash.\n327\t\n328\t**EC-09 Same sha pushed by two boxes in the same epoch window.** Ref name collision is benign (same content); the push is verify-then-skip. Cross-box lease files don't exist — each box GCs only refs it created (lease records are local).\n329\t\n330\t## Invariants (CI-enforced, not prose)\n331\t\n332\t- **INV-1 No silent skip:** every invocation ends in a terminal record or a detectable orphaned intent. (SIGKILL test in Phase 1 acceptance.)\n333\t- **INV-2 No branch mutation:** gantry never moves a branch ref; asserted via `git ls-remote` diff in e2e tests.\n334\t- **INV-3 Exit-code fidelity:** the caller's exit code always reflects the verdict; verdicts derive from status APIs, never from parsing log text.\n335\t- **INV-4 Passthrough budget:** <5ms p99 (hyperfine in CI; regression = build failure).\n336\t- **INV-5 Argv round-trip:** byte-exact through shim → JSON → remote argv (property test).\n337\t- **INV-6 Network confinement:** no connections except the configured backend and git remote (S-7 test).\n338\t- **INV-7 No local retry of real failures:** `test_failure` and `gate_failure` never trigger a local rerun.\n339\t\n340\t## Security considerations\n341\t\n342\t- **S-1 no implicit branch pushes** (DD-2) — the predecessor's worst incident class.\n343\t- **S-2 repo config is untrusted**: `.gantry.toml` cannot alter push targets, backends' credentials, or command templates. Only user/system config can define executable command templates.\n344\t- **S-3 no credential storage**: backends use ambient credentials (kubeconfig file path, SSH agent, git credential helpers). Gantry never reads/writes tokens.\n345\t- **S-4 arg hygiene** (DD-7): args as arrays end-to-end; remote receives `args_json`; no shell interpolation anywhere.\n346\t- **S-5 log hygiene**: run records store the remote URL as given but never credentials embedded in URLs (strip userinfo before logging).\n347\t- **S-6 published threat model**: `docs/notes/threat-model.md` states what gantry can and cannot touch — ref-leak surface, untrusted repo config, credential posture — and ships alongside the public README.\n348\t- **S-7 no-phone-home, as a test**: an integration test asserts the binary opens no network connections except the configured backend and the git remote; the pledge is CI-enforced, not prose.\n349\t\n350\t## Risk register\n351\t\n352\t| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |\n353\t|---|------|-----------|--------|------------|\n354\t| R1 | Phase 1 scope exceeds estimate (17 adopted mechanisms) | High | High | Walking skeleton + 1a/1b split below; scope lock; 1b is the cut list if 1a slips |\n355\t| R2 | Epoch-ref naming vs content-addressing tension surfaces late | Medium | High | Design note is a Phase 1a *entry* deliverable, settled before RefPusher is built |\n356\t| R3 | Cold remote builds slower than local (sccache cold/absent) → adoption stalls | Medium | High | `doctor --e2e` measures round-trip; expectations documented; Tier-0 keeps the tool valuable regardless |\n357\t| R4 | kubectl dependency/version skew breaks argo backend | Medium | Medium | doctor preflight pins minimum kubectl; REST client remains the stretch escape |\n358\t| R5 | No systemd on target (containers, macOS) weakens caps | Medium | Medium | Documented degrade to plain exec; Q-5 open; doctor reports active cap tier |\n359\t| R6 | Argo output-param cap truncates failure tails | Medium | Medium | Q-6 open; watermarked truncation; artifact channel benched in ledger |\n360\t| R7 | Shared-worktree fleet semantics diverge from single-checkout assumptions | Medium | High | EC-01 + two-worktree stampede variant + Phase 3 fleet-cycle audit |\n361\t| R8 | `refs/gantry/*` propagate through server-side push mirrors to public GitHub | Medium | High | Interim: docs recommend a dedicated `ci_remote` for mirrored repos; mirror-leak guard benched (owner-skipped) |\n362\t| R9 | flock semantics unreliable on network filesystems | Low | Medium | State dir MUST be local disk; doctor verifies |\n363\t\n364\t## Quality gates (definition of done)\n365\t\n366\t`rust-toolchain.toml` is pinned at the repo root from the first commit of Phase 0.5. No phase completes — and no release ships — unless all of the following pass **on the same commit**:\n367\t\n368\t1. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n369\t2. `cargo test` (unit + property + stampede suites relevant to the phase)\n370\t3. hyperfine passthrough budget (INV-4) within target\n371\t4. The phase's acceptance list green\n372\t5. From Phase 3 on: no-phone-home test (INV-6) green in CI\n373\t\n374\tA regression in any gate is a build failure, not an advisory. Gantry's own CI dogfoods the remote contract as soon as Phase 2 lands.\n375\t\n376\t## Implementation phases\n377\t\n378\tEach phase names its entry criteria (the prior phase's quality gates) and a rough size estimate — honesty devices, not commitments.\n379\t\n380\t### Phase 0 — Repo, docs, contract ✅\n381\tScaffold, research, features, decisions, plan.\n382\t\n383\t### Phase 0.5 — Walking skeleton (~800 LOC)\n384\t**Goal:** prove the wiring end-to-end; everything may be crude, panics allowed. Shim dispatch on argv[0] → GitGate happy path → epoch-ref push → `command` backend running a bash executor on the same box → verdict → correct exit code. One hardcoded config; no semaphore, no doctor.\n385\t**Exit criterion:** one real `cargo test` round-trips through the shim to a local \"remote\" and back with the right exit code, for both a passing and a failing suite.\n386\t\n387\t### Phase 1a — Core loop, hardened (~2,500 LOC)\n388\t**Entry:** skeleton exit criterion met; epoch-vs-content-addressing design note written and settled.\n389\tConfig layering + last-known-good + trust boundary, full GitGate with reasons, RefPusher with leases + GC sweep, `argo` backend, complete verdict ladder (incl. `gate_failure`), write-ahead RunLog with gate-input capture, `GANTRY_LOCAL`/`on`/`off`, `doctor` core checks.\n390\t**Acceptance (AS-1, AS-4):** on a clean repo, `cargo test` runs remotely with streamed logs and correct exit codes for pass/fail; dirty repo falls back with reason; pod-never-scheduled falls back locally (not exit 1); `cargo test -- \"weird: [args]\"` round-trips intact (property suite, INV-5); passthrough overhead < 5 ms (hyperfine, INV-4); no branch ref moves on the remote (`git ls-remote` assert, INV-2); SIGKILLing gantry mid-run leaves an orphaned intent that `doctor` reports (INV-1); a corrupted config file produces last-known-good behavior + banner, never silence.\n391\t\n392\t### Phase 1b — Safety rails & explainability (~2,000 LOC)\n393\t**Entry:** Phase 1a quality gates green.\n394\tFallback admission semaphore, boxwide `gantry.slice` sum cap, `GANTRY_AGENT` priority queueing, Tier-0 zero-config mode + `gantry quickcheck`, flight-recorder bundles + `gantry report`, `gantry why`/`explain` (+ `--json`).\n395\t**Acceptance (AS-2, AS-3):** 20 simultaneous fallback invocations serialize through the semaphore (stampede test, including the two-worktree variant per EC-01); Revision history lives in git; decision provenance in `docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md`.*\n\n## Overview\n\n`gantry` is a transparent offload shim for expensive developer commands, cargo-first. A shim binary named `cargo` sits ahead of the real toolchain in PATH; when an intercepted subcommand (default: `test`) is run inside a clean, pushable git repo, gantry ships the exact commit to a pluggable remote executor, streams logs back, and returns a faithful exit code. In every other case it runs the command locally under a cgroup resource cap. Callers — humans, scripts, AI agent fleets — never change what they type.\n\nExtraction and hardening of the in-house `~/.local/bin/cargo` + `cargo-remote` bash pair (see `docs/research/in-house-implementation.md`); packaging follows the single-static-binary + installer + `doctor` pattern surveyed in `docs/research/prior-art.md`.\n\n## Goals\n\n1. Drop-in transparency: `cargo test` keeps working everywhere, with zero caller-side changes.\n2. Never lose a test result: every invocation ends in a real verdict (remote or capped-local), every degradation is printed and logged.\n3. Never mutate branch state: code sync uses hidden content-addressed refs only.\n4. Pluggable remote execution: Argo Workflows first-class, generic command-template backend for everyone else, SSH later.\n5. Protect the shared machine: production-proven cgroup caps on all local execution paths.\n6. Publishable quality: single static binary, installer, `doctor`, docs that stand alone without this infrastructure.\n\n## Non-goals\n\nCompilation caching (compose with sccache), hermetic/Bazel-style execution, dirty-tree syncing, per-agent hook integrations, Windows, nextest interception (v1). See `docs/notes/features.md` for rationale.\n\n## Terms & conventions\n\n**Normative language:** MUST / MUST NOT are binding — violating them fails this spec. SHOULD means deviation requires a documented reason. MAY is truly optional.\n\n**Glossary** (two uses of \"gate\" exist; they are different things):\n- **shim** — the binary installed under the name `cargo`, ahead of the real toolchain in PATH.\n- **intercepted / passthrough** — an invocation gantry may offload vs. one it forwards untouched (under the cap when `cap_passthrough`).\n- **GitGate** — the *eligibility* checks (work tree, HEAD, remote, clean) deciding remote vs. local. Never called just \"gate\" in output.\n- **quality gate** — an opt-in remote check beyond the caller's argv (clippy, fmt), always labeled `[gantry] gate:` and carrying verdict `gate_failure` when failed.\n- **verdict** — the terminal classification of a run (`pass` / `test_failure` / `gate_failure` / `infra_failure` / `cancelled` / `superseded`). The exit code is derived from it, never vice versa.\n- **Tier-0** — zero-config mode: cap-only, nothing goes remote.\n- **backend / preset** — a `RemoteBackend` implementation vs. a shipped configuration of one (SSH is a preset of `command`).\n- **fallback / degradation** — the loud, recorded switch to a capped local run after an infra failure or gate ineligibility.\n- **epoch ref / lease** — `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` plus the client-side record that protects it from GC while a run is live.\n- **attachment / waiter** — a process streaming/waiting on a run (originator or JoinTable joiner).\n\n**Scope lock:** v1 scope is frozen as of 2026-07-22 (17 adopted mechanisms; see Resolved questions). New scope enters only via the ideation ledger → plan amendment → commit, *before* implementation of that item begins. In-flight scope additions are forbidden — this plan doubled in mechanism count across two productive ideation days precisely because the pipeline works; the freeze is what makes Phase 1 finishable.\n\n## Acceptance scenarios\n\nNamed scenarios define \"done.\" Each is independently verifiable; phase acceptance lists reference them.\n\n**AS-1 Happy path (human).** A developer in a clean, pushed-up repo runs `cargo test`. → gantry pushes the epoch ref, submits, streams logs live, prints the verdict trailer. → Exit 0 on pass.\n*Pass:* zero caller-side changes; logs stream within 30s of submit or a queue explanation prints; exit code equals what local `cargo test` would have produced.\n*Fail:* any branch ref moved on the remote; silence >60s with no `[gantry]` line; exit code differs from the suite's true result.\n\n**AS-2 Agent machine-mode (primary audience).** A NEEDLE worker (`GANTRY_AGENT=1`) runs `cargo test` on a wip branch; the suite has one failing test. → Remote runs, verdict `test_failure` with `failure_class: test-failure`. → The worker runs `gantry why --json` and branches on the failure class without parsing logs.\n*Pass:* transcript contains the decision line, verdict trailer, and handle; `why --json` parses with a stable schema and names the failure class; the worker never needed a human.\n*Fail:* worker must regex the log stream to learn what happened; JSON schema drifts between invocations; a gate failure is indistinguishable from a test failure.\n\n**AS-3 Cluster outage under fleet load.** 20 agents run `cargo test` while the backend is unreachable. → Every run prints the infra reason, acquires a fallback slot (max 3 concurrent), and runs capped locally; the rest queue loudly.\n*Pass:* box load stays bounded (slice cap holds); every run ends in a real verdict; runs.jsonl shows 20 intent+verdict pairs with `ran: local_after_infra`.\n*Fail:* simultaneous uncapped local builds (the meltdown gantry exists to prevent); any run exits with neither verdict nor orphan record.\n\n**AS-4 Dirty tree.** A developer with an uncommitted new test file runs `cargo test`. → GitGate blocks remote (untracked file detected), prints the reason and the exact two-command path to eligibility, runs capped locally.\n*Pass:* the untracked file's tests actually ran (locally); reason `dirty` recorded; no ref pushed.\n*Fail:* remote runs against code missing the new file (the predecessor's silent-gap bug); user must read docs to learn why it ran locally.\n\n**AS-5 Gate failure attribution.** Gates enabled (fleet config); tests pass but clippy fails. → Exit non-zero with verdict `gate_failure`, output attributing the failure to `[gantry] gate: clippy`, tests reported green.\n*Pass:* an agent reading `why --json` sees tests-passed-gate-failed and fixes lints, not tests.\n*Fail:* gate failure presented as a test failure (misdirected agent work), or gates-off runs affected in any way.\n\n**Success metrics:** *Performance* — passthrough <5ms p99; submit overhead (gate+push+submit, excluding queue) ≤5s p50. *Functionality* — AS-1..AS-5 pass. *Adoption* — one week of NEEDLE traffic with zero silent skips and ≥90% of eligible runs offloaded; bash pair deleted.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\ncaller (human / agent / script)\n   │  runs `cargo test …`\n   ▼\n[shim dir]/cargo ──symlink──► gantry binary\n   │  argv[0]=cargo → tool profile \"cargo\"\n   ├─ subcommand not intercepted ───────────────► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n   ├─ GANTRY_LOCAL=1 / disabled / Tier-0 (no config) ──► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n   ▼\nDecisionEngine\n   ├─ GitGate: work tree? remote? clean (porcelain)? HEAD?\n   │     └─ any \"no\" → LocalExecutor (reason printed)\n   ▼\nRefPusher: git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>  (+ lease, + GC sweep)\n   ▼\nBackend (trait RemoteBackend)\n   ├─ argo:    create Workflow(templateRef, params) → stream pod logs → poll status.phase\n   ├─ command: run user-templated submit/logs/wait argv arrays\n   └─ ssh preset: command-template preset + contrib/gantry-exec.sh (flagship onboarding)\n   ▼\nVerdict\n   ├─ Pass ──────────────► exit 0\n   ├─ TestFailure ───────► exit code (no local retry — DD-4)\n   ├─ GateFailure ───────► exit non-zero, attributed to `[gantry] gate:` (no retry)\n   └─ InfraFailure ──────► LocalExecutor (capped) → real cargo\n                                   │\n                          RunLog (~/.local/state/gantry/runs.jsonl)\n```\n\nCross-cutting: `RunLog` records every decision; `Locks/JoinTable` (v1.x) dedups concurrent identical runs; `doctor` validates the whole chain.\n\n## Components\n\n### 1. Shim & dispatcher (`main.rs`)\n- Dispatch on `argv[0]`: `cargo` → cargo tool profile; `gantry` → management CLI (full command set defined once in the “CLI surface” section below).\n- Real-binary resolution: config override `real_binary`, else PATH lookup with gantry's own shim dir stripped (self-recursion guard: refuse to exec a path whose canonical target is the gantry binary).\n- Passthrough path budget: no git/network/config-parse beyond a single mmap'd config read; target < 5 ms overhead.\n\n### 2. DecisionEngine\n- Intercept set from config (`[tool.cargo] intercept = [\"test\"]`).\n- Tier-0 (zero-config): with no config file present or `backend = \"none\"`, gantry is a pure local cap-wrapper — interception still applies the cgroup cap and full RunLog, nothing goes remote, and a `[gantry]` line notes the tier at most once per hour (state-file timestamp) so transcripts see it without per-run noise. Install→value with zero setup; remote offload is an upgrade, not a prerequisite.\n- Kill switches: `GANTRY_LOCAL=1`, `gantry off` (state file).\n- Config-failure policy (resolves Q-7 via last-known-good): on parse failure, serve the persisted last-good config snapshot from the state dir and print an escalating `[gantry] config broken since <ts>, N runs degraded` banner on every intercepted run until fixed; with no snapshot, fail open to plain passthrough with the same banner. Behavior is never derived from a half-parsed file — a broken gantry must never block builds, and must never rot silently either.\n\n### 3. GitGate\n- Checks in order, each with a printed reason on failure: inside work tree → `HEAD` resolves → configured remote exists → `git status --porcelain` empty.\n- All git interaction shells out to system `git` (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior, honors user's git config/credentials/hooks).\n\n### 4. RefPusher\n- `git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` (`ci_remote` defaults to `origin`); the epoch prefix is the GC lever (see below).\n- Push failure = InfraFailure → local fallback.\n- Optional `push_mode = \"branch\"` legacy escape hatch (explicit opt-in; prints a warning naming the risk).\n- GC (resolves Q-3 via leases): refs are named `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`; each run records a client-side lease (ref, run-id, expiry) in the state dir, and every successful push opportunistically sweeps remote refs whose epoch has expired and whose runs are terminal — no cron, no daemon, and a sweep can never delete a ref an in-flight run still holds a lease on. Each box sweeps only refs it created — lease records are local (see EC-09). The epoch-vs-content-addressing tension (the same sha pushed twice yields two refs) is settled by the design note required at Phase 1a entry.\n\n### 5. RemoteBackend trait + implementations\n\n```rust\ntrait RemoteBackend {\n    fn submit(&self, spec: &RunSpec) -> Result<RunHandle, BackendError>;\n    fn stream_logs(&self, h: &RunHandle, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<(), BackendError>; // best-effort\n    fn wait(&self, h: &RunHandle, deadline: Instant) -> Result<Verdict, BackendError>;     // authoritative\n    fn describe(&self, h: &RunHandle) -> String;  // human URL/name for \"see details at …\"\n    fn cancel(&self, h: &RunHandle) -> Result<(), BackendError>;                            // Ctrl-C propagation\n}\n```\n\n- **`argo`** (v1): builds the Workflow manifest with serde (no string splicing), submits via `kubectl create -f -` (kubeconfig path from config; direct REST API is a later option), polls pods for streaming, polls `status.phase` for the verdict, falls back to reading `outputs.parameters.output` when podGC ate the logs. Ships `contrib/argo/gantry-verify-workflowtemplate.yml` — a genericized `rust-verify` (parameters: `repo`, `revision`, `args-json`, `builder-image`; sccache optional). Remote contract (resolves Q-2 as faithful-argv): the remote executes exactly the argv the caller typed; check/clippy run only as opt-in quality gates from trusted user config, reported as separately-labeled `[gantry] gate:` results, never conflated with the test verdict. A failing enabled gate yields verdict `gate_failure`: overall exit is non-zero (agents must see red), output and records attribute it to the named gate, and — like TestFailure — it never triggers a local retry. The template also emits a structured `verdict.json` output parameter — one versioned schema (`schema_version`, phase, exit code, oom, deadline from workflow node status, plus an optional `failure_class`: compile-error vs test-failure vs doctest vs harness-panic, derived from cargo's stable `--message-format json` stream) — so OOMKilled and deadline-exceeded classify as InfraFailure → fallback, never TestFailure, and agents branch on failure class without parsing logs. Consumers ignore unknown fields; an absent verdict.json degrades gracefully to exit-code-only interpretation (command templates). Parity preflight: builder images carry capability labels (`org.gantry.toolchain=…`); before submission gantry compares local rust-toolchain.toml and requested features against them — a mismatch is a loud local fallback (warn-only for unlabeled images), because a verdict from the wrong toolchain is a wrong answer delivered confidently.\n- **`command`** (v1): three user-configured argv arrays (`submit`, `logs`, `wait`) with `{repo}` `{rev}` `{args_json}` `{handle}` placeholder substitution at the argv level; `submit`'s stdout is the handle; `wait`'s exit code is the verdict (0 pass, 1 test-failure, ≥2 infra-failure — documented contract).\n- **SSH-first onboarding** (v1, flagship): not a third backend implementation — a shipped command-template *preset* plus `contrib/gantry-exec.sh` (~150-line POSIX executor that clones `refs/gantry/*` and runs the command), which doubles as executable documentation of the remote contract. \"Remote = any spare SSH box\" is the documented quickstart path; Argo is the \"advanced\" backend. A native `ssh` backend remains possible later only if the preset proves limiting.\n\n### 6. LocalExecutor\n- `systemd-run --scope --user -p CPUQuota={n}% -p MemoryMax={m} -p MemorySwapMax=0 -q -- <real> <args…>`; on failure to create a scope (no user session / container), plain `exec`.\n- Applies to: intercepted-command fallbacks always; all passthrough invocations when `cap_passthrough = true` (default, matching predecessor).\n- Fallback admission semaphore: capped local *fallback* runs additionally acquire a flock-based token file (default 3 concurrent per box) and queue with loud `[gantry] waiting for local slot (N ahead)` lines and a bounded wait — a remote outage under ~20 agents degrades as a serialized trickle, not a stampede that recreates the meltdown gantry exists to prevent. Kernel lock release means a SIGKILLed agent can never leak a slot.\n- Boxwide slice: every gantry-spawned local run lands in one systemd user slice (`gantry.slice`) carrying a box-level *sum* cap (configurable, e.g. 12 CPU / 32G) alongside the per-run caps — the semaphore bounds the count, the slice bounds the total; 20 × \"200%/6G each\" can no longer add up past the machine. Degrades cleanly where slices are unavailable.\n- Agent-priority queueing: `GANTRY_AGENT=1` (env convention — deliberately not TTY sniffing, since tmux-hosted agents have TTYs) orders the fallback-semaphore queue humans-first, agents-behind, with a printed triage tag (any future submission gating inherits the same ordering).\n\n### 7. RunLog & UX\n- stderr lines prefixed `[gantry]`: decision, workflow name/URL, fallback reason, verdict. Written for agent transcripts as much as humans.\n- `~/.local/state/gantry/runs.jsonl`: write-ahead form — an OPEN intent record is appended *before* dispatch, and every exit path must append a matching terminal verdict record; `gantry doctor` flags orphaned OPEN records as lost runs, making a silently-skipped run structurally detectable rather than an absence of evidence. O_APPEND single-line writes for concurrency safety.\n- Intent records capture all gate inputs (tree state, remote, kill-switch state, chosen backend) so `gantry why` can replay the decision truthfully after the fact.\n- Flight recorder: every InfraFailure snapshots a redacted diagnostic bundle (config snapshot, git state, raw backend response, recent stderr) to `~/.local/state/gantry/crash/<run-id>/`; `gantry report <run-id>` prints or packages it. Infra flakes become post-mortem-able artifacts instead of archaeology; the redaction list is load-bearing and conservative by default.\n\n### 8. doctor / installer\n- `gantry doctor`: shim-before-real PATH ordering; real binary resolves and is not gantry; config parses; backend preflight (`kubectl` reachable / template exists, or command-backend binaries exist); systemd-run scope creation probe; git identity present; orphaned intent records reported as lost runs.\n- `gantry doctor --e2e`: canary run — pushes a tiny known-good fixture ref through the real RefPusher and backend and asserts the expected pass verdict round-trips. One command answers \"is the pipeline actually working\" on the operator's schedule, not at 9am when 20 agents degrade. Mechanism: pushes the current repo's HEAD as a normal gantry ref but overrides the argv with a trivial command (`cargo --version`), exercising push → clone → contract → verdict without running a real suite; `gantry init --ssh` runs it as its final step.\n- `gantry doctor --drill`: fault-injection fire drill — injects a synthetic InfraFailure through a drill-scoped hook (never honored outside a drill) and asserts the entire loud-degrade chain fires: banner, intent/verdict records, semaphore-gated capped local run, correct exit code. The fallback path is gantry's core safety promise and otherwise only executes when things are already on fire.\n- `install.sh`: detect platform → fetch release binary → install to `~/.local/bin/gantry` → create shim symlink(s) in a configured shim dir → verify PATH ordering (instruct if wrong) → write starter config → run `doctor`. `gantry uninstall` reverses it.\n- Onboarding must be smooth and automatic: `gantry init --ssh user@host` performs the whole SSH-first setup — verifies git+cargo on the target, writes the command-template preset config, and finishes with `doctor --e2e`. Install to first remote run in ~10 minutes, no Kubernetes required.\n\n### 9. JoinTable (v1.x)\n- Key: `(remote_url, sha, tool, args)` hash. A flock'd state dir maps in-flight keys → RunHandle; a second invocation attaches to the existing handle (stream + wait) instead of resubmitting.\n\n### 10. Ledger intelligence (v1.x)\nOne verdict-history module over runs.jsonl powering three features:\n- **Memoization (opt-in, never default):** an identical `(tree-hash, args, toolchain, image digest)` with a terminal PASS verdict returns the recorded verdict instantly with a `[gantry] cached` line and a `--fresh` escape. Keyed on tree hash, not commit sha, so rebases/amends with identical trees still hit. Failures are never memoized.\n- **Supersede-on-new-commit:** a newer sha submitted for the same (repo, args) cancels the older still-running sibling with an explicit `superseded` terminal record — recorded, never silent — reclaiming cluster minutes from fast-iterating agents. Supersede never yanks a watched run: it applies only when the older run has zero live attachments (originator gone, no JoinTable waiters); otherwise the newer sha simply runs alongside.\n- **Flake flagging:** the same tree + args with flipping verdicts marks runs `flaky-suspect` in runs.jsonl and the stderr summary.\n\n### Proposed module layout\n\n```\nsrc/main.rs            argv[0] dispatch only\nsrc/shim.rs            passthrough fast path (<5ms budget lives here)\nsrc/decision.rs        intercept set, Tier-0, kill switches\nsrc/gate.rs            GitGate\nsrc/refs.rs            RefPusher: epoch refs, leases, GC sweep\nsrc/backend/mod.rs     RemoteBackend trait + verdict.json parsing\nsrc/backend/argo.rs    kubectl-based Argo backend\nsrc/backend/command.rs command-template backend (SSH preset = config + contrib script)\nsrc/local.rs           LocalExecutor: scope, slice, semaphore, priority\nsrc/runlog.rs          write-ahead ledger, flight recorder\nsrc/config.rs          layering, last-known-good, trust boundary\nsrc/cli/               doctor, why, explain, init, quickcheck, report, status…\ncontrib/argo/          reference WorkflowTemplate\ncontrib/gantry-exec.sh shell reference executor\ntests/properties/      argv round-trip, ref-name fuzzing\ntests/stampede/        20-way concurrency harness\ntests/e2e/             drill + canary fixtures\n```\n\n## Data models\n\n### Config — `~/.config/gantry/config.toml` (layered: /etc/gantry → user → repo `.gantry.toml`)\n\n```toml\n[local]\ncpu_quota_pct = 200\nmemory_max    = \"6G\"\ncap_passthrough = true\n\n[tool.cargo]\nintercept   = [\"test\"]\n# real_binary = \"/home/user/.cargo/bin/cargo\"   # optional override\n\n[remote]\nbackend    = \"none\"          # none = Tier-0 cap-only (zero-config default) | argo | command\nci_remote  = \"origin\"\npush_mode  = \"ref\"           # ref | branch (legacy, warns)\ndeadline_minutes = 40\n\n[remote.argo]\nkubeconfig = \"~/.kube/config\"\nnamespace  = \"argo-workflows\"\ntemplate   = \"gantry-verify\"\ngenerate_name = \"gantry-\"\n\n[remote.command]\n# submit = [\"my-ci\", \"submit\", \"--repo\", \"{repo}\", \"--rev\", \"{rev}\", \"--args\", \"{args_json}\"]\n# logs   = [\"my-ci\", \"logs\", \"{handle}\", \"--follow\"]\n# wait   = [\"my-ci\", \"wait\", \"{handle}\"]\n```\n\nRepo-level `.gantry.toml` may narrow behavior (add intercepts, set `backend = \"none\"`) but may **not** change `ci_remote`/`push_mode`/credential-adjacent keys — repo config is data from the repo, and a cloned repo must not be able to redirect pushes (security consideration S-2).\n\n### RunSpec / RunRecord\n\n```rust\nstruct RunSpec { tool: String, subcommand: String, args: Vec<String>,\n                 repo_url: String, sha: String, cwd_rel: PathBuf }\n```\n\n`cwd_rel` is the caller's directory relative to the repo root; remote executors `cd` into it before running the argv, so workspace-member invocations behave identically remote and local.\n\n```rust\n// runs.jsonl — write-ahead: one OPEN intent + one terminal record per invocation\n{ \"rec\": \"intent\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"run_id\": \"01J…\", \"ts\": …,\n  \"tool\": \"cargo\", \"args\": [\"test\",\"--\",\"--nocapture\"], \"repo\": \"…\", \"sha\": \"…\", \"cwd_rel\": \".\",\n  \"gate\": { \"worktree\": true, \"head\": true, \"remote\": true, \"clean\": true },\n  \"decision\": \"remote|local\", \"reason\": \"clean|dirty|no_remote|tier0|disabled|env\",\n  \"backend\": \"argo|command|none\" }\n{ \"rec\": \"verdict\", \"schema_version\": 1, \"run_id\": \"01J…\", \"ts\": …,\n  \"verdict\": \"pass|test_failure|gate_failure|infra_failure|superseded|cancelled\",\n  \"ran\": \"remote|local|local_after_infra\", \"exit_code\": 0, \"handle\": \"gantry-x7k2p\",\n  \"durations_ms\": { \"gate\": 40, \"push\": 900, \"queue\": 12000, \"run\": 341000 } }\n```\n\n### Verdict semantics (the load-bearing enum)\n\n| Verdict | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| `Pass` | remote ran suite, passed | exit 0 |\n| `TestFailure` | remote ran suite, failed | exit non-zero; **no local retry** |\n| `InfraFailure` | no verdict produced (push/submit/schedule/stream/deadline) | capped local run; its exit code wins |\n\nOOMKilled pods and deadline-exceeded workflows are `InfraFailure` by definition (via the remote contract's `verdict.json`): an infrastructure cap firing says nothing about the code, and reporting it as a test failure would fake a result.\n\nTerminal-record values extend the ladder: `gate_failure` (an enabled quality gate failed while tests passed — exit non-zero, attribution to the named gate, no local retry), `cancelled` (user Ctrl-C), and `superseded` (v1.x, see Ledger intelligence). `verdict` applies to local runs too (`ran: \"local\"`); an infra fallback records the final local outcome as `ran: \"local_after_infra\"`.\n\n### Versioning & compatibility\n\nEvery machine-consumed surface carries an explicit version; unknown fields are always ignored (additive evolution is free, removal/retyping is a major bump):\n\n- **runs.jsonl** — `schema_version` on every record. Readers MUST tolerate newer minor records; `gantry doctor` flags a ledger written by a newer major.\n- **verdict.json** — `schema_version`; absent file = exit-code-only contract. Optional fields (`failure_class`) are exactly that.\n- **`--json` CLI output** (`why`/`explain`/`status`) — top-level `schema_version`; the JSON surface is the primary interface, human text is a rendering of it.\n- **Remote contract** — the client sends `contract_version` as a workflow parameter; the template echoes it in verdict.json. A mismatch the client can't interpret = InfraFailure with an explicit \"contract drift\" message, never a misread verdict. Template upgrades are blue-green: `gantry-verify` versions coexist and the client config pins one.\n- **Config** — unknown keys warn (never error); renamed keys keep a one-major deprecation alias; the last-known-good snapshot stores the schema version it parsed under.\n- **Backward-compat stance for the predecessor:** cap values and nextest non-interception match the bash pair exactly; behavioral differences (porcelain gate, epoch refs, OOM classification) are deliberate fixes, listed in the migration notes — there is no bug-for-bug mode.\n\n## CLI surface\n\n```\ncargo <anything>            # via shim — the entire point\ngantry doctor [--e2e|--drill]        # verify install; canary the real pipeline; fire-drill the fallback chain\ngantry init --ssh user@host          # automatic SSH-first onboarding (preset + contrib executor + e2e check)\ngantry why                  # replay the last run's gate/decision trace (\"clean tree: NO ← here\")\ngantry explain -- <cmd…>    # dry run: what WOULD happen (gates, backend, exact ref) — no network\ngantry on | off             # global toggle (state file)\ngantry run [--backend B] -- <cmd…>   # explicit offload, no shim needed (v1.x)\ngantry status               # recent runs, in-flight runs\ngantry quickcheck           # 30s no-backend sanity: shim resolves, cap works, git ok (Tier-0 proof)\ngantry report <run-id>      # print/package the flight-recorder bundle for an InfraFailure\ngantry install-shims | uninstall\ngantry config [--show-origin]\ngantry version\n```\n\nDiagnostics are agent-first: `why`, `explain`, and `status` take `--json` with a stable schema, so a fleet agent that hits a degradation can explore and self-diagnose (why did this run locally? is the remote down for everyone?) without a human reading stderr.\n\n## Failure modes (exhaustive, each with defined behavior)\n\n| Failure | Class | Behavior |\n|---|---|---|\n| not a git repo / no remote / dirty / untracked files | eligibility (GitGate) | local capped run, reason printed |\n| ref push rejected (auth, network) | infra | local capped run |\n| submit error (kubectl/exec fails) | infra | local capped run |\n| pod never scheduled by deadline | infra | **local capped run** (predecessor wrongly exited 1) |\n| log stream lost mid-run | infra (recoverable) | keep waiting on status; fetch output param at end |\n| client deadline (`deadline_minutes`) exceeded | infra | print handle URL, local capped run |\n| remote suite fails | test | exit non-zero, stop |\n| enabled quality gate fails (tests pass) | quality-gate | exit non-zero, verdict `gate_failure` attributed to the named gate; no local retry |\n| remote pod OOMKilled / workflow `activeDeadlineSeconds` exceeded | infra | `verdict.json` classifies as InfraFailure → capped local run — never reported as a test failure |\n| gantry process killed mid-run | self | orphaned OPEN intent in runs.jsonl; `gantry doctor` reports it as a lost run |\n| remote outage → mass fallback | env | admission semaphore caps concurrent local runs (default 3), loud queue-position lines |\n| Ctrl-C during remote run | user | propagate `cancel()`, exit 130 |\n| gantry config broken/missing | self | serve last-known-good snapshot + escalating banner; plain passthrough if no snapshot (never silent) |\n| systemd-run unavailable | env | plain exec (documented: containers self-limit) |\n| gantry binary deleted but shim remains | self | shim *is* the binary (symlink) — impossible state; doctor checks dangling links |\n\n## Edge case catalog\n\n**EC-01 Linked git worktrees (load-bearing: NEEDLE workers share worktrees).** All GitGate checks and pushes operate on the *worktree's* HEAD and index. JoinTable and memoization keys use the common git dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) + sha, so two worktrees of one repo dedup correctly. A stampede-test variant MUST run from two worktrees of the same repo.\n\n**EC-02 Detached HEAD.** Eligible — a sha is a sha. The decision line notes `(detached)`; nothing else differs.\n\n**EC-03 Submodules.** If `.gitmodules` exists, v1 falls back locally with reason `submodules` (the remote clone contract doesn't recurse yet). Loud, honest, and cheap; recursion is a template upgrade later.\n\n**EC-04 Shallow local clone.** Push of the epoch ref may fail against a shallow history → ordinary push InfraFailure → capped local run. No special handling; the reason line names the likely cause.\n\n**EC-05 Huge repo / slow status.** `git status --porcelain` on a monorepo can take seconds. Gate duration is recorded (`durations_ms.gate`) and a `[gantry] slow gate (Ns) — consider .gitignore hygiene` hint prints past 2s. The gate is never skipped for speed.\n\n**EC-06 Pathological argv.** NULs are impossible in argv; newlines/quotes/100KB args MUST round-trip byte-exact (property test, tests/properties/). Args are never shell-interpolated anywhere (S-4).\n\n**EC-07 Cargo aliases and bare `cargo`.** Interception matches argv[1] exactly against the intercept set. Aliases expanding to `test` inside real cargo are NOT intercepted (documented limitation — gantry never parses cargo config to chase aliases).\n\n**EC-08 State dir unwritable / disk full.** Never blocks the build: run proceeds with in-memory records, one warning line, and `doctor` reports the unwritable state dir. A full disk MUST NOT turn into a missing verdict or a crash.\n\n**EC-09 Same sha pushed by two boxes in the same epoch window.** Ref name collision is benign (same content); the push is verify-then-skip. Cross-box lease files don't exist — each box GCs only refs it created (lease records are local).\n\n## Invariants (CI-enforced, not prose)\n\n- **INV-1 No silent skip:** every invocation ends in a terminal record or a detectable orphaned intent. (SIGKILL test in Phase 1 acceptance.)\n- **INV-2 No branch mutation:** gantry never moves a branch ref; asserted via `git ls-remote` diff in e2e tests.\n- **INV-3 Exit-code fidelity:** the caller's exit code always reflects the verdict; verdicts derive from status APIs, never from parsing log text.\n- **INV-4 Passthrough budget:** <5ms p99 (hyperfine in CI; regression = build failure).\n- **INV-5 Argv round-trip:** byte-exact through shim → JSON → remote argv (property test).\n- **INV-6 Network confinement:** no connections except the configured backend and git remote (S-7 test).\n- **INV-7 No local retry of real failures:** `test_failure` and `gate_failure` never trigger a local rerun.\n\n## Security considerations\n\n- **S-1 no implicit branch pushes** (DD-2) — the predecessor's worst incident class.\n- **S-2 repo config is untrusted**: `.gantry.toml` cannot alter push targets, backends' credentials, or command templates. Only user/system config can define executable command templates.\n- **S-3 no credential storage**: backends use ambient credentials (kubeconfig file path, SSH agent, git credential helpers). Gantry never reads/writes tokens.\n- **S-4 arg hygiene** (DD-7): args as arrays end-to-end; remote receives `args_json`; no shell interpolation anywhere.\n- **S-5 log hygiene**: run records store the remote URL as given but never credentials embedded in URLs (strip userinfo before logging).\n- **S-6 published threat model**: `docs/notes/threat-model.md` states what gantry can and cannot touch — ref-leak surface, untrusted repo config, credential posture — and ships alongside the public README.\n- **S-7 no-phone-home, as a test**: an integration test asserts the binary opens no network connections except the configured backend and the git remote; the pledge is CI-enforced, not prose.\n\n## Risk register\n\n| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |\n|---|------|-----------|--------|------------|\n| R1 | Phase 1 scope exceeds estimate (17 adopted mechanisms) | High | High | Walking skeleton + 1a/1b split below; scope lock; 1b is the cut list if 1a slips |\n| R2 | Epoch-ref naming vs content-addressing tension surfaces late | Medium | High | Design note is a Phase 1a *entry* deliverable, settled before RefPusher is built |\n| R3 | Cold remote builds slower than local (sccache cold/absent) → adoption stalls | Medium | High | `doctor --e2e` measures round-trip; expectations documented; Tier-0 keeps the tool valuable regardless |\n| R4 | kubectl dependency/version skew breaks argo backend | Medium | Medium | doctor preflight pins minimum kubectl; REST client remains the stretch escape |\n| R5 | No systemd on target (containers, macOS) weakens caps | Medium | Medium | Documented degrade to plain exec; Q-5 open; doctor reports active cap tier |\n| R6 | Argo output-param cap truncates failure tails | Medium | Medium | Q-6 open; watermarked truncation; artifact channel benched in ledger |\n| R7 | Shared-worktree fleet semantics diverge from single-checkout assumptions | Medium | High | EC-01 + two-worktree stampede variant + Phase 3 fleet-cycle audit |\n| R8 | `refs/gantry/*` propagate through server-side push mirrors to public GitHub | Medium | High | Interim: docs recommend a dedicated `ci_remote` for mirrored repos; mirror-leak guard benched (owner-skipped) |\n| R9 | flock semantics unreliable on network filesystems | Low | Medium | State dir MUST be local disk; doctor verifies |\n\n## Quality gates (definition of done)\n\n`rust-toolchain.toml` is pinned at the repo root from the first commit of Phase 0.5. No phase completes — and no release ships — unless all of the following pass **on the same commit**:\n\n1. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n2. `cargo test` (unit + property + stampede suites relevant to the phase)\n3. hyperfine passthrough budget (INV-4) within target\n4. The phase's acceptance list green\n5. From Phase 3 on: no-phone-home test (INV-6) green in CI\n\nA regression in any gate is a build failure, not an advisory. Gantry's own CI dogfoods the remote contract as soon as Phase 2 lands.\n\n## Implementation phases\n\nEach phase names its entry criteria (the prior phase's quality gates) and a rough size estimate — honesty devices, not commitments.\n\n### Phase 0 — Repo, docs, contract ✅\nScaffold, research, features, decisions, plan.\n\n### Phase 0.5 — Walking skeleton (~800 LOC)\n**Goal:** prove the wiring end-to-end; everything may be crude, panics allowed. Shim dispatch on argv[0] → GitGate happy path → epoch-ref push → `command` backend running a bash executor on the same box → verdict → correct exit code. One hardcoded config; no semaphore, no doctor.\n**Exit criterion:** one real `cargo test` round-trips through the shim to a local \"remote\" and back with the right exit code, for both a passing and a failing suite.\n\n### Phase 1a — Core loop, hardened (~2,500 LOC)\n**Entry:** skeleton exit criterion met; a toolchain-mismatched image is refused with a loud local fallback (warn-only when unlabeled).\n\n### Phase 3 — Onboarding, packaging & migration (mostly packaging/docs; ~600 LOC)\n**Entry:** Phase 2 quality gates green, template live on the reference cluster.\nmusl static build; config reproduces current behavior (argo backend → `rust-verify` initially); NEEDLE fleet inherits via PATH with zero changes; keep bash scripts as `.bak` for one week; watch `runs.jsonl` across a fleet cycle.\n**Acceptance:** one week of NEEDLE production traffic with no silently-skipped runs (audit runs.jsonl vs worker transcripts) and no branch pushes originating from gantry; curl-pipe install on a fresh box reaches a passing `quickcheck` with zero config; `gantry init --ssh` against a clean host ends with `doctor --e2e` green; the no-phone-home test is green in CI.\n\n### Phase 4 — Fleet features (v1.x)\n**Entry:** Phase 3 migration acceptance met (fleet is on gantry).\nJoinTable dedup, ledger intelligence (opt-in memoization, supersede-on-new-commit, flake flagging), `gantry run`, `gantry status`, crates.io publish (name pending — open question Q-1). Check at publish time; fallbacks `gantry-rs` (matches the repo) / `gantry-shim`. Repo name stays `gantry-rs` regardless; binary stays `gantry`.\n- **Q-4 `builder-image` selection.** A repo-chosen image is remote code execution with the CI pod's credentials (sccache keys, clone tokens) — an arbitrary image named in `.gantry.toml` would gut S-2. The in-house config keeps the gates on.\n- **Q-3 → lease-based GC.** Epoch-named refs (`refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`) plus client-side leases; every push opportunistically sweeps expired, terminal refs. No cron, no daemon; sweeps can never race an in-flight clone.\n- **Q-7 → last-known-good.** Broken config serves the persisted last-good snapshot with an escalating banner (plain passthrough + banner if no snapshot exists). Never silent, never blocking, never derived from a half-parsed file.\n\nAlso adopted in that run (finalists 1–9 of 10; finalist 10, the demo/exit-code-oracle fixture, was declined): verdict.json infra-classification, write-ahead intent ledger, fallback admission semaphore, SSH-first onboarding with automatic `gantry init --ssh` and agent-first `--json` diagnostics, `gantry why`/`explain`, `doctor --e2e`/`--drill`.\n\nRun 2 (2026-07-22) adopted: Tier-0 zero-config cap-only mode + `quickcheck`, ledger intelligence (v1.x), parity preflight with image capability labels, boxwide `gantry.slice` sum cap, `GANTRY_AGENT` priority convention, verdict.json v2 failure taxonomy, flight-recorder crash bundles + `gantry report`, threat-model doc + CI-enforced no-phone-home pledge.
